description: An additive synth voice: one of fourteen partial-generating algorithms, an internal envelope, and up to 128 partials summed into a single output

params.text: Picks which of the fourteen algorithms is generating the partials; the four letters on the display above say which one
The first of the two parameters belonging to the chosen algorithm; what it does changes with the algorithm, from the spread of the partials to a random seed
The second of the two parameters belonging to the chosen algorithm; what it does changes with the algorithm, from fading between even and odd partials to the depth of a phase modulation
Sets how much of the jack below it moves the algorithm selection, inverted anticlockwise of centre and none at centre
Sets how much of the jack below it moves the first algorithm parameter, inverted anticlockwise of centre and none at centre
Sets how much of the jack below it moves the second algorithm parameter, inverted anticlockwise of centre and none at centre
Sets how long the internal envelope takes to rise
Sets how long the internal envelope takes to fall
In one position the envelope holds at the gate's own voltage for as long as the gate is up, and in the other it starts falling as soon as it has risen
Sets how much of the FM jack reaches the frequency, inverted anticlockwise of centre and none at centre
Sets how many partials are calculated, doubling from one at the far left to 128 at the far right
Applies a progressively tighter envelope to the higher numbered partials, so the sound darkens as it dies away; none at the far left
Tunes the oscillator, three octaves either side of centre; the reading is in semitones

inputs.text: Steps through the fourteen algorithms; with nothing patched it reads the internal envelope, squared and scaled to 10V, so the algorithm is swept by the envelope itself
Shifts the first algorithm parameter; with nothing patched it reads the internal envelope, squared and scaled to 10V
Shifts the second algorithm parameter; with nothing patched it reads the internal envelope, squared and scaled to 10V
Sets the pitch at one volt per octave, 0V giving C4
Modulates the frequency exponentially, scaled by the knob beside it; with nothing patched it reads an internal sine at the oscillator's own fundamental, so the knob alone gives feedback
Opens the internal envelope. Its voltage is taken as the level to open to, so it doubles as a velocity input; with nothing patched the envelope is held fully open and the module drones

outputs.text: The summed partials, soft clipped at 10V

notes: O-Tamer is an expander for this module and goes immediately to its LEFT; it filters the partials, chooses what replaces the removed ones, and sends out the internal envelope
The maker's tooltip on the algorithm selection jack reads Gate, which is a mistake in the source; the gate jack itself is the unnamed one at the bottom of the panel

inputs.0:
±5V · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads the internal envelope squared, up to 10V.
inputs.1:
±5V · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads the internal envelope squared, up to 10V; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to ±1V.
inputs.2:
±5V · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads the internal envelope squared, up to 10V; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to ±1V.
inputs.3:
1V per octave · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads 0V.
inputs.4:
bipolar · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads an internal sine at the oscillator's fundamental.
inputs.5:
0 to 10V · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads fully open; a negative voltage does nothing here.
